conditions: cases in or near the training set

statement.excerpt: Notice anything? It’s not just that the performance on MathGLM steadily declines as the problems gets bigger, with the discrepancy between it and a calculator steadily increasing, it’s that the LLM based system is generalizing by similarity, doing better on cases that are in or near the training set, never, ever getting to a complete, abstract, reliable representation of what multiplication is.
statement.document_title: “Math is hard” — if you are an LLM – and why that matters

our_interpretation: Assess the MathGLM experiments discussed in the post, rather than later models.
Read 'steadily declines' primarily as a consistent downward trend; separately report whether every successive digit length declines.
Treat calculator performance as an ideal exact-arithmetic reference within the tested domain, not as a measured device benchmark.
The similarity mechanism and absence of an abstract representation are separate empirical assertions. Error rates alone cannot establish them.
Use September 2023, the reporting month of the paper discussed, as the target period.
criteria.support_condition: The reported size-dependent results show the claimed decline, and controlled training-distance tests or analysis of the model's computations establish similarity dependence and failure to acquire the asserted reliable abstraction.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Matched results overturn the downward trend, or model-specific analysis demonstrates a reliable multiplication procedure that generalizes independently of proximity to training examples. A local accuracy increase contradicts only a strictly monotonic reading.
